summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of post-polio syndrome, CAD s/p CABG, and depression was admitted for generalized weakness and recurrent falls. She presented after calling EMS due to severe weakness and fear of falling, with recent psychosocial stressors including the loss of her husband and pet. Evaluation revealed a urinary tract infection with E. coli on culture, despite being asymptomatic for typical urinary symptoms. She was treated with IV ceftriaxone and transitioned to oral cefpodoxime. Mild pulmonary edema was noted on imaging but required no intervention. Her anemia and thrombocytopenia remained at baseline. Blood cultures remained negative. Physical therapy recommended inpatient rehabilitation for deconditioning, which the patient accepted. She was discharged to an extended care facility with plans to complete her antibiotic course, continue home medications including sertraline for depression, and follow up on pending concerns with her PCP.
